book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook usually defines cooperative banks, gives their history and then the structure (short-term rural tiers and urban banks) and regulators in a list. Here the definition is a scene (a local community starts a bank that serves the same community), objectives follow, and the commercial bank is placed beside it as a mirror (owners vs users). Before any structure, a full worked village example shows in rupees why a community would do this (better deposit and loan rates, reserves kept, still a small profit shared as dividend). Then the structure is built bottom-up from empty tier slots (tier 1 first, then district, then state), registration comes as the learner's own question ('which office do I go to?'), and the regulators enter one by one as each need appears (society needs a registrar; bank needs a licence; health needs inspection), ending in a grid whose dual and triple control sets up the next video.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Start from who owns and who is served, prove the benefit with one worked money example, then build the structure bottom-up and add each regulator only when a need calls for it, ending in a summary grid that poses the next problem.

opening.what: States the topic, then defines a cooperative bank through a small scene: whenever people of a local community together start a bank so that it serves that same community with loans, deposits and other services, it is called a cooperative bank; the screen draws the community, a 'starts' arrow to a bank and a 'banking services' arrow back to the same crowd.

talmel_summary: In the definition and the worked example the picture carries the meaning: a closed loop (community starts a bank that serves the same community) beside a commercial bank whose small shareholder group serves a big public, then the village money flow built step by step as it is spoken (100 people split off, pooled money flows in, a 100-lakh bar cut into lend / SLR / CRR, each slice routed with its yield, 25 borrowers branching off) and a tally that ends in +58 thousand. The structure is built bottom-up with a fixed colour per bank type, and the regulator coverage is readable from rows of squares (4, 3, 2) and a YES staircase. Weak: the 'promotes' list, UCB facts, who-serves-whom notes and the Registrar's powers are text that copies the speech, and the tally table appears whole before its rows are read. 15 of 24 tiles land together; picture leads are short except the tally (5-22 s before its rows). No tile falls in a transcript gap.

voice.notes: About 188 words per minute, friendly and explanatory. Numbers read in lakh and crore with 'each' doubled in Hindi ('teen-teen lakh', which speech recognition turned into '33 lakh'); percentages plain (4%, 12%, 10%, 5%). The commercial bank speaks in first person ('main aapko 4% dunga'), and the registration part is asked in first person ('main kaun se office mein jaun?'). Acronyms are said letter by letter (PCS, UCB, DCCB, RCS). Slightly faster in the structure part.

game_ideas.player_does: Starts a village co-op bank with 100 members who pool 1 lakh each. Keeps CRR and SLR as RBI requires, then sets the deposit rate, the loan rate and how much to lend to members who ask for loans, against a commercial bank offering 4% and 12%.
game_ideas.process_happens: The 100-lakh bar splits into CRR (to RBI at 0%), SLR (into bonds at 6%) and the lending slice; loans flow to the borrowers; at year end the tally fills: loan interest and bond interest in green, expenses and deposit interest in pink, and the profit (or loss) is shared as dividend.
game_ideas.win: Members are better off than with the commercial bank (deposit rate above 4%, loan rate below 12%) and the tally ends at zero or above.
game_ideas.lose: Paying 6% on deposits and lending at 8% turns the tally red; skipping CRR/SLR brings an RBI penalty notice.
game_ideas.concept: worked village example: 100 members, 1 crore, CRR/SLR, loans at 10%, deposits at 5%, profit 58,000

game_ideas.player_does: Builds a state's cooperative structure: drops PCS and UCB squares into district frames, places DCCBs and the state bank, then draws service arrows down the tree.
game_ideas.process_happens: Each correct placement lights its tier band; service arrows animate money support from the state bank to DCCBs to the societies below.
game_ideas.win: One DCCB per district, one state bank per state, every society connected to support.
game_ideas.lose: A second DCCB in the same district is refused with 'one per district'; an unlinked PCS shows 'no source of support'.
game_ideas.concept: district and state tiers (DCCB, state cooperative bank) and who serves whom

game_ideas.player_does: Matches each regulator (RCS, RBI, NABARD) to the bank types it covers, then counts regulators per type.
game_ideas.process_happens: YES marks fill the grid into a staircase; types with two regulators get a 'dual control' brace, three a 'triple control' brace, and a short reason pops for each link (licence, inspection, registration).
game_ideas.win: Grid correct and the dual and triple control labels placed on the right rows.
game_ideas.lose: Putting PCS under RBI shows 'no banking licence, so not under RBI'; putting UCBs under NABARD shows the all-India workload reason.

checks_learned: A running money example must balance: parts sum to the whole (75 + 18 + 4 + 3 = 100 lakh) and the tally equals its rows (7.5 + 1.08 - 3 - 5 = 0.58 lakh); worked here, enforce in code.
Number checks that compare transcript and screen must understand Hindi 'each' doubling ('teen-teen lakh' heard as '33 lakh'), so a false alarm is not raised and a real mismatch is not missed.
A worked example must say whether members' money is a deposit (earns interest) or share capital (earns dividend); here the same 1 crore is treated as both.
Leftover cash and yearly expenses are different things; 'the remaining 3 lakh is spent on expenses' should be flagged as a stock-flow mix-up.
Structural claims (UCBs under DCCBs, UCBs serving PCS) must be checked against the book source.
Regulatory facts must carry an 'as of' date (the 2020 Banking Regulation amendment changed RBI's powers over co-op banks); 'NABARD regulates' should read 'supervises/inspects' if the book says so.
Real bank logos used as characters must be replaced by generic bank marks.
A list with a moving highlight should not hold one canvas for over about 30 s; each item gets a small scene or the list is cut.
One colour per entity type kept through the whole video (worked here: yellow PCS, orange UCB, dark green DCCB, light green state bank); enforce as a scene check.
A table of results should reveal row by row as each row is spoken, not all at once 5-20 s early.

teaching_best.why: The definition is a scene and a loop picture (a community starts a bank that serves the same community), so owner = customer is seen before the term is said.
The commercial bank is a mirror of the same picture: a small shareholder group owns it and a big public is served; goal 'profit' vs 'not profit'.

One complete worked example with numbers that balance: reserves as slices of the same money, rates compared with the commercial bank, a tally to +58 thousand, and what each member gains (better deposit rate, cheaper loan, dividend).
The structure is built bottom-up into empty tier slots with a fixed colour per bank type and counts like 'one per district', 'one per state'.
Registration is reached through the learner's own question ('which office do I go to?'), and each regulator enters only when a need appears (a bank needs a licence, so RBI).
A consolidation grid turns the regulators into a YES staircase and names dual and triple control, which sets up the next video's problem.

teaching_weak.why: About 80 s on one canvas with a four-item list and a moving highlight; abstract claims with no picture of participation or inclusion.
Leftover cash is 'spent on expenses' and the members' 1 crore earns both deposit interest and dividend; the example blurs deposit and capital.
UCB facts arrive as a note box, a conditions list and a members card: text-heavy.
Who-serves-whom is told by text notes, and the claim that UCBs sit under DCCBs and serve PCS is doubtful.
The Registrar's powers are a six-item text list.
Dual and triple control is presented without the 2020 amendment that changed RBI's powers; NABARD is said to 'regulate' where it inspects.
Real bank logos used for the commercial bank and the co-op bank.
